items.title: What will Apple’s John Ternus era look like?
items.summary: It’s officially the Ternus era at Apple. Tim Cook stepped down as CEO this week, handing the company to former hardware chief John Ternus, whose first memo promised a “huge launch next week” — timing that puts Apple’s next iPhone event on his desk before he’s even settled in. Cook isn’t going far, though: he’s staying on as Executive Chairman, focused on the kind of policy […]

items.title: No little kids allowed, and other new info about Tesla’s Cybercab
items.summary: The company says no children under 13 can ride -- even with a parent. That's more restrictive than the Model Y SUVs it's using as robotaxis.

items.title: Another swarm of OpenAI agents reached the open internet without the frontier lab’s knowledge
items.summary: It's the latest failure of OpenAI's internal monitoring and security systems.

items.title: CD sales are making an unexpected comeback amid a retro tech boom
items.summary: U.S. CD revenue jumped 58.6% in the first half of 2026, reversing last year’s decline as interest in retro tech and physical media continues to grow.

items.title: Roland is getting into generative AI music with Melody Flip
items.summary: It's not quite the "push button; get song" of Suno, but Roland's new Melody Flip tool marks the company's foray into generative AI music. Available as a plug-in for your digital audio workstation (DAW), Melody Flip offers around 250 "Palettes," which are essentially themed collections of musical ideas sorted by genre. items.title: Microsoft says virtually nobody was grabbing NYT articles through its chatbot
items.summary: Microsoft's Copilot rarely reproduces even full sentences from news articles and books, let alone substantive chunks that could substitute for the original, the company says in new legal filings as it fights copyright claims from publishers including The New York Times and book authors.
